At the Store
Most Americans make one or more trips to the grocery
store every week.  Some people consider grocery shopping
a form of entertainment, but others regard it as a chore.  No
matter how you feel about shopping, a few strategies can
make your investment of time worthwhile.
Shop the perimeter—The freshest foods generally are
located along the perimeter of the store.  These include
fresh fruits, vegetables, breads, dairy products, and meats.
Choose whole-grain breads from the bakery, low-fat products
from the dairy section, and lean cuts from the meat section.
Higher-fat foods often are stocked in the interior of the
store.  However, grains, legumes, pastas, and canned fruits
and vegetables also are frequently located in the interior.
Shop from your list—A list helps ensure that you stick
to your plan.  Items purchased on impulse generally are
more expensive and less nourishing than foods from a well-
planned shopping list.
Do not shop when hungry—If you go to the store
with a growling stomach, you are apt to make purchases to
satisfy your immediate hunger rather than what you will
need in the days ahead.  You also tend to buy more.
Shopping on a full stomach helps you stick to your list and
to keep your resolve.
Make bargains count—A bargain is only a bargain
when you buy what you want rather than what someone else
is trying to sell you.  Select bargains that fit your menu, such
as in-season fruits and vegetables or bulk quantities of rice,
beans, and legumes.  Use coupons to reduce the cost of
foods that you intend to buy.
